learning_outcomes.text: Understand the use of numerical tools available to design engineers for structural dynamics.
Be able to build a simple dynamic numerical model.
Understand a technical report created using finite element software.
Understand seismic prevention of structures and buildings.
Acquire the skills needed to use numerical tools such as the finite element method, specifically in structural dynamics.
Know about the seismic resources available to civil engineers, whether for buildings or engineering structures such as bridges.

syllabus_topics: Numerical calculation methods for structural dynamics used in design offices. Overview of the various calculation methods available to the engineer: modal analysis, time and frequency responses.
Introduction to modal analysis, modal parameters and response by modal superposition, regulatory seismic analysis in civil engineering using response spectra.
Non-linear dynamic analysis: progressive thrust method, analysis using implicit and explicit formulations.
Final mini-project for the study of a prestressed reinforced concrete bridge, linear approaches on a modal basis, by response spectrum then implicit nonlinear, with calculation report.
Seismic prevention of structures and buildings, case studies.
assessment_rules: Evaluation is based on a study report from the final mini-project, which is carried out in pairs using the finite element method (Abaqus).
